class.name: WorkerTaskQueue
class.brief_description: Multithreaded FIFO of tasks on worker threads of its own.
class.description: Runs submitted [Callable]s on [code]max(processor count - 2, 1)[/code] worker threads of its own, started with the first task - never Godot's [WorkerThreadPool], which the engine's own loading waits for: a task there that waits for the main thread (a mesh read back from the [RenderingServer]) deadlocks it. A task may submit further tasks and [method wait] for them: the waiting thread runs the awaited task itself while it is still queued, so nested waiting does not deadlock. A finished task is announced on the main thread ([signal task_finished]), so the main thread awaits it rather than asking [method is_done] every frame. Used by [code]SceneryInstancer[/code] to parse every scenery include as a separate task, by [SceneryStreamingServer] to preload what it streams, and to read vehicle profiles. Queued tasks are dropped when the queue is freed; the queue must not be freed by its own task.

method.name: drain
method.description: Drops the queued tasks, announcing each with [signal task_finished], and joins the workers, finishing what they run. Call it while the scene tree is still alive: a task is GDScript, which goes away with the tree. A [method wait] for a dropped task returns [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_submitted_count
method.description: Number of tasks submitted so far, including those submitted by other tasks.

method.name: is_done
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the task has finished and its result can be taken with [method wait] without blocking.

method.name: submit
method.description: Queues [param task] ([code]task() -> Variant[/code]) and returns its id.

method.name: wait
method.description: Returns the result of the task and forgets it. A task still queued is run by the calling thread; one running on a worker is waited for, the calling thread asleep until it is done.

signal.name: task_finished
signal.description: A task finished, or was dropped by [method drain]. Emitted on the main thread once the frame's deferred calls run, so whoever awaits it right after [method submit] hears it.
